documents.body: Canadian banks / Bank of Montreal BMO: U.S. returns must earn the valuation premium Credit normalization and capital efficiency are rebuilding earnings. At more than twice July common book, the share price also requires lasting improvement in the return on capital committed to the U.S. franchise. TickerLantern Research 25 October 2026 Financials: quarter ended 31 July 2026 Watchlist · return recovery already matters Can the U.S. franchise lift returns on total equity after the credit comparison becomes harder? Our FY2027 modeled EPS of C$17.15 and 13.5× exit P/E imply C$231.53 in October 2027 and a +0.6% cash-dividend-inclusive return. This is a conditional valuation case. The case at a glance CAD Reference close C$236.87 12-month model value C$231.53 FY2027 EPS · our model C$17.15 Base total return +0.6% Price: 23 October 2026 Financials: 31 July 2026 Analysis: 25 October 2026 Evidence confidence: high for cited actuals; forecasts are judgment. Underwriting: watchlist / scenario research. Bank of Montreal — TSX historical price · Daily historical data Source posture Issuer reported and issuer-adjusted results stay distinct. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and review flags are TickerLantern assumptions. No licensed consensus feed or point-in-time valuation backtest is represented. Investment case A return recovery with a demanding entry price ↑ BMO offers exposure to a recovery in the earnings power of a large North American banking franchise. The investment question is how much further the return on shareholder capital can improve once easier credit comparisons fade. At the October 23 close of C$236.87 , the shares trade at an analyst-calculated 16.47× trailing adjusted EPS and 2.10× July book value . The former uses FY2025 adjusted EPS of C$12.16 plus nine-month FY2026 EPS of C$11.11, less the comparable C$8.89: a C$14.38 trailing measure. Neither the price nor the multiple describes an undiscovered turnaround. Our valuation test separates business progress from the return available to a new shareholder. Faster profit growth can coexist with a disappointing share return if the starting multiple already capitalizes the improvement. A book-value cross-check makes that burden visible: with 4% perpetual growth and a 9.5% equity cost, the observed book multiple implies a sustainable ROE of approximately 15.5%. Raising the equity cost to 10% increases the required ROE to approximately 16.6%. These are stylized steady-state inferences, not price targets. The favorable case requires deposits and fee relationships to deepen while lending produces acceptable returns after losses. A lower share count can help per-share earnings, but it cannot repair weak economics on the capital that remains deployed. We would become more constructive if recurring returns advance without greater credit risk or a higher valuation multiple. We would become less constructive if the recovery needs persistent reserve relief, unusually strong markets, or repeated disposals to meet the earnings path. Bank of Montreal — TSX historical price · Daily historical data BMO Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025 Results · Table 2, adjusted results and EPS BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 Earnings quality Read the operating recovery beside the accounting charges ↑ Q3 FY2026 reported EPS was C$2.38 , against C$3.96 adjusted ; reported and adjusted ROE were 8.4% and 14.0%. Divestiture-related goodwill reductions explain much of that divergence. Our nine-month bridge attributes the C$1.409 billion increase in adjusted income to C$1.210 billion higher pre-provision profit, C$655 million lower credit provisions and C$456 million higher tax. Performing allowances account for C$439 million of the credit improvement. The calculation supports an operating recovery, while also identifying a benefit that should not automatically recur. Adjusted earnings are useful for forecasting the continuing business because they remove specified accounting and transaction items. They also require economic judgment. Excluding an acquisition-related goodwill charge does not reimburse shareholders for the original purchase price. An analysis that accepts the recurring earnings benefit but ignores the capital loss gives an incomplete account of value creation. We therefore use adjusted common income for the earnings model, and retain reported book value and capital allocation as independent tests. The forecast should start with actual nine-month results and an explicit fourth-quarter estimate. Annualizing the best quarter can quietly embed favorable trading activity, seasonal effects and lower preference-share distributions into every future period. Each forecast change should have a named driver: revenue, expense, impaired losses, performing allowances, taxes or shares. Earnings quality improves when ordinary customer activity carries more of the growth and the need for adjustments narrows. A widening reported-to-adjusted gap would warrant a lower confidence rating even if headline adjusted EPS meets our estimate. BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 Franchise and returns The U.S. franchise must earn back its capital burden ↑ The Bank of the West transaction was announced at US$16.3 billion and completed in February 2023. Its strategic promise was scale and a broader customer base; its economic test is the return earned on all capital committed. U.S. Banking's Q3 adjusted ROE was 9.8% . A return measured after excluding acquisition goodwill can be materially different from the return on total common equity. The distinction matters: attractive returns after removing goodwill do not establish that the total acquisition investment has earned its cost. We underwrite the U.S. opportunity through customer economics. Commercial borrowers can support payments, treasury and wealth relationships, making the total relationship more valuable than a standalone loan spread. The bank must convert that potential into durable operating deposits and fees. Growing loans faster than relationship funding can weaken the funding mix, increase marginal costs and expose the franchise to a less forgiving credit cycle. Headline balance growth is therefore insufficient evidence of success. Canada, wealth and capital markets can generate capital and soften a weak U.S. period, but their strength also creates a temptation to overlook the largest remaining return gap. Capital-market activity and wealth fees share exposure to market conditions; they are not independent cushions in every downturn. Our base case should normalize strong market earnings rather than compound them indefinitely. The franchise earns a stronger premium when U.S. returns rise through deeper relationships and better productivity while the established businesses sustain their economics. If U.S. returns stall after credit costs normalize, the case for a higher group multiple weakens. BMO announces Bank of the West acquisition · Purchase price and strategic rationale BMO Completes Acquisition of Bank of the West · Opening announcement BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 Credit and capital Track loss formation and capital released, separately ↑ Q3 credit provisions were C$722 million : C$708 million impaired and C$14 million performing. The total loss rate was 41 basis points; CET1 was 13.0%. These figures are starting observations, not through-cycle forecasts. The key distinction is between losses on borrowers already in difficulty and changes in expected losses on performing exposures. A quieter allowance quarter can improve profit without proving that new problem-loan formation has stopped. Our credit thesis requires evidence across several quarters: stable formations, manageable watch-list migration, cash recoveries and losses consistent with the risk embedded in new lending. A falling impaired-loan balance alone is insufficient because write-offs and loan sales can also reduce it. Commercial files can make quarterly losses uneven, so a single favorable quarter should not set the terminal loss assumption. Stress cases should combine weaker revenue, higher impaired losses and renewed performing allowances rather than vary only one benign input. Portfolio exits introduce another distinction. BMO completed the 138-branch sale in September; the Transportation and Vendor Finance sale was announced with a retained minority interest. Exiting lower-return assets can improve capital efficiency, but the foregone income must leave the earnings forecast. Capital released becomes valuable only through productive reinvestment or disciplined distributions. We would not add a full capital benefit, retain all disposed earnings and assume unchanged funding costs. The clean test is whether recurring common earnings per dollar of equity improve after transaction effects settle. A rising capital ratio with declining per-share earning power would be weaker evidence than the ratio alone suggests. BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 BMO Completes Sale of 138 U.S. Branches · Opening announcement BMO Announces Strategic Sale of Transportation and Vendor Finance · Capital efficiency and retained minority interest Dividends and buybacks Cash returns help, but the repurchase price matters ↑ The declared quarterly dividend is C$1.71 , payable November 26 to holders of record October 30. Annualizing that declaration gives C$6.84, a 2.89% yield at the reference price and approximately 47.6% of our trailing adjusted EPS measure. The annualized dividend is a convention, not a promise of future payments. Its contribution to total return is meaningful, but a low earnings multiple or an attractive entry price cannot be inferred from dividend continuity alone. The September authorization permits up to 25 million share repurchases through September 7, 2027. It is permission to buy, not proof of execution. The approval release identified 695.1 million shares outstanding at August 31. Our model must reconcile future share reductions with the cash and equity spent to achieve them. Buying above book value can increase EPS while reducing book value per remaining share; whether that creates value depends on the return the repurchased earnings stream offers compared with other uses of capital. The Moneris agreement adds a separate capital event: BMO expects an approximately C$600 million after-tax gain and roughly 15 basis points of CET1 benefit on closing, anticipated by the end of Q1 FY2027. We exclude that gain from recurring earning power. Sale proceeds, accounting gains and free capital are different quantities. Our preferred distribution policy retains capacity for credible lending opportunities and adverse credit outcomes, then repurchases shares when their prospective return is attractive. Maximizing the near-term EPS lift would be a weaker objective than improving long-term value per share. BMO Declares Fourth Quarter 2026 Dividends · Common dividend and payment dates Bank of Montreal — TSX historical price · Daily historical data BMO Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025 Results · Table 2, adjusted results and EPS BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 BMO Receives Regulatory Approvals for Normal Course Issuer Bid · Approval, share counts and prior purchases BMO Announces Sale of Moneris · Consideration, expected gain and CET1 benefit MODEL A linked operating forecast through FY2028 ↑ Forecasts begin with the issuer-adjusted nine months actually reported. We add an independently assumed Q4, then grow revenue and expenses separately, set credit provisions and tax, deduct non-common claims, and divide common earnings by diluted shares. Every FY2026 full-year column therefore contains an estimate. No forecast in this table is bank guidance or Street consensus. The assumptions that drive the result The Q4 assumption is C$9.9bn revenue and C$5.4bn expense, slightly below Q3, allowing for disposed branch economics and normalization of activity. The model does not preserve all exited-business earnings and add a separate disposal gain. Net transaction and funding effects remain embedded in these aggregate assumptions. FY2027 revenue grows about 4.7% and expense about 2.4%. Positive operating leverage and lower PCL do meaningful work. That is an explicit execution hurdle, not an extrapolation of every Q3 improvement. The Moneris gain is excluded from recurring earning power. Credit charges of C$2.65bn and C$2.6bn, a 24% tax rate, and diluted shares of 690m and 680m are independent assumptions. Share reductions require capital spending; this model does not forecast the complete CET1 and common-equity bridge. Stress results should be read alongside capital disclosures. Pretax = revenue − expenses − insurance service expense (where applicable) − PCL. Common earnings = pretax × (1 − tax rate) − additional after-tax charge − preferred, other equity and non-controlling claims. FY2026 shares use a 3:1 weighting of nine-month diluted shares and Q4 assumed shares; this is an equal-quarter approximation, not an exact day-weighted issuer calculation. Rounded table cells do not control the calculation. Download linked forecast CSV Download sources and model inputs BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 BMO Completes Sale of 138 U.S. Branches · Opening announcement BMO Announces Sale of Moneris · Consideration, expected gain and CET1 benefit BMO Receives Regulatory Approvals for Normal Course Issuer Bid · Approval, share counts and prior purchases VALUE What must the stock earn from this starting price? ↑ Our primary bank method values sustainable common EPS directly. Deposits, cash and wholesale funding are operating inputs for banks, making a conventional industrial-company enterprise-value bridge a poor central method. There is no additional cash windfall or buyback yield added to the EPS valuation. The EPS bridge combines rounded per-share periods with changing share counts. It is a transparent comparable anchor, not a fresh single-denominator annual EPS filing. Our forward estimate comes from the operating model above. We use a deliberately chosen exit multiple rather than presenting a historical average as intrinsic value. Three operating cases, one 12-month horizon Model value by scenario · CAD per common share The vertical line marks the dated entry price. Dividends are shown in the table, outside the price values plotted here. A 13.5× base P/E values the improving recurring earnings stream while asking for evidence that U.S. returns on total equity can continue rising. The bear case pairs credit pressure with 11.5×, and the bull case allows 15× for better persistence. These choices are research judgments, not a claim that BMO historically trades inside this range. These cases are unweighted. They are neither a probability distribution nor confidence intervals. The bear case explains one loss mechanism; it does not bound losses in a severe solvency, regulatory or market shock. Future dividends can change. No return is guaranteed. BMO Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · Tables 1–5, 8–9 and 12; printed pp. 7–12, 15–19 BMO Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025 Results · Table 2, adjusted results and EPS Bank of Montreal — TSX historical price · Daily historical data STRESS Separate the earnings risk from the multiple risk ↑ Credit sensitivities apply an extra annual charge to a fixed C$697.93bn loan proxy: 31 July 2026 net loans, a period-end balance rather than an average. This is a transparent stress denominator, distinct from the issuer’s average-loan and day-count convention. A 10 bp increase costs 698 million before tax; the model tax rate converts it to common earnings. No balance-sheet growth or second-round capital response is included. Credit provisions and valuation can deteriorate together. A table holding P/E constant understates that joint downside; the bear scenario explicitly lowers both earnings and the multiple. Review flags below trigger a new analysis rather than an automatic trade. ROE Cross-check the franchise premium with common book ↑ A stable-state residual-income identity provides a second lens: justified P/B = (sustainable ROE − growth) / (cost of equity − growth). It assumes common-equity clean surplus, constant profitability and payout, and cost of equity above growth. It excludes transition years and is not a bank appraisal. At our 15% ROE / 10% cost / 4% growth assumptions 1.83× book C$207.28 applied to current common book ROE implied by the dated price / current common book 16.6% Conditional on the same cost-of-equity and growth assumptions Our 15% sustainable ROE assumption already builds in improvement from Q3’s 14%. At 10% equity cost and 4% growth it implies approximately 1.83× book, below the observed 2.10×. A lower cost of equity or stronger sustainable profitability would close the gap. Tangible ROE cannot be inserted in a formula using total common book without changing the economic definition. Sustainable ROE (%) Cost of equity (%) Perpetual book growth (%) Common BVPS (CAD) Justified P/B 1.83× Current-book cross-check C$207.28 Price-implied sustainable ROE — Growth is financed by retaining earnings: implied payout = 1 − growth / ROE. Assumptions implying growth above ROE or growth at or above the cost of equity are rejected. Buybacks above common book can lift EPS while reducing BVPS; accounting book is not a sum-of-parts liquidation value. LAB Change the valuation and operating assumptions ↑ The valuation lab edits the numerator, exit multiple and cash dividend independently. Loading a case uses its linked operating EPS; a manual EPS entry is your own assumption. The separate operating stress tool starts from the base model and does not silently rewrite the lab. Bear case Base case Bull case Reset valuation Entry price (CAD) FY2027 diluted EPS (CAD) Exit P/E (×) 12-month cash dividends (CAD) October 2027 model value C$231.53 Total return with cash dividends +0.6% Entry for 10% modeled return C$216.70 Download current scenario CSV Return = (exit EPS × exit P/E + cash dividends − entry price) / entry price. The 10% entry price is (model value + dividends) / 1.10. It holds the future outcome fixed; it does not predict a trading opportunity or imply that a lower quotation leaves earnings unchanged. Operating stress calculator Revenue change vs base (%) Expense change vs base (%) Extra annual credit cost (bp) Stressed FY2027 EPS C$17.15 Return at unchanged base P/E +0.6% Extra pre-tax credit charge C$0m Tax rates, shares and non-common claims are fixed in this local stress. A loss is shown as negative EPS; the simple P/E price-value calculation is floored at zero when earnings turn negative and becomes economically uninformative. A real capital assessment would then be essential. RETURN Five years: earnings growth can be offset by a lower multiple ↑ Starting from issuer-adjusted TTM EPS, this separate illustration compounds earnings for exactly five years, transitions to the chosen exit P/E and pays year-end cash dividends. It does not extend the detailed FY2027–2028 operating forecast. Annual EPS growth, dividend growth and the exit multiple are independent reader assumptions. Starting price (CAD) Starting adjusted TTM EPS (CAD) Annual EPS growth (%) Year-five exit P/E (×) First-year dividend (CAD) Annual dividend growth (%) Annualized cash-flow return (IRR) +5.3% Year-five price + uninvested dividends C$303.02 Illustrative price plus accumulated cash per initial share Cash-flow IRR discounts each annual dividend and the year-five sale price to the initial purchase. Accumulated cash earns zero interest and is not reinvested. Intermediate chart prices use the final exit P/E in every year for illustration, so the chart is not a price forecast. Taxes, costs, splits, currency changes and default are excluded; no historical relationship is estimated. Catalysts and falsifiers Execution must outpace what the valuation already assumes ↑ The next scheduled earnings checkpoint is December 2, 2026 . The useful catalyst is a result that changes expected sustainable earning power, rather than a disposal gain that was already anticipated. We will examine whether stronger relationships support revenue after portfolio exits, expenses grow more slowly than recurring revenue, and U.S. returns improve without larger performing-allowance releases. The next operating checkpoint is evidence that the U.S. business can lift recurring returns on total equity after credit and transaction effects normalize. Better business performance still needs an attractive entry valuation to create a strong investment return. A stronger outcome would combine durable deposit and fee growth, disciplined credit selection and productive capital redeployment. That combination can support both faster EPS growth and greater confidence in the earnings multiple. A weaker outcome could begin with modest operating disappointment and become more severe if investors simultaneously demand a higher equity return. This is why the scenario model must vary earnings and valuation together. A bank can remain profitable and well capitalized while its shares decline substantially as the market removes a premium. Our thesis would need revision if U.S. return improvement stalls after credit normalization, core costs outrun revenue, or strong market businesses conceal disappointing customer-banking economics. Trade disruption could affect commercial borrowers on both sides of the border; funding competition can pressure margins before a clear deterioration appears in credit losses. Transaction execution and minority investments add further uncertainty. We would also challenge the favorable case if capital release is repeatedly needed to sustain distribution targets. The evidence that would change our view is explicit: recurring return on total equity, realized common-income growth and disciplined purchase prices for both acquisitions and the bank's own shares. BMO Investor Relations — Presentations and Events · FY2026 earnings conference-call dates PEERS Compare business economics before comparing P/E ↑ All four new articles use the same 23 October price date and July-quarter financial period. The original RBC article retains its own 16 October quotation and 18 October analysis. Issuer adjustments remain bank-defined; different accounting, geography, insurance and divestiture treatments prevent a clean consensus ranking. BMO’s key gap is the return earned on equity committed to the U.S., including acquisition goodwill. A premium to Scotiabank or CIBC cannot be justified simply by a large U.S. footprint; its normalized credit, deposits and capital efficiency must support the earnings attached to that footprint. These are common-equity research cases, not a diversified portfolio. Canadian mortgages, employment, commercial borrowing and global capital markets can affect several banks simultaneously. Cross-border earnings create additional currency and regulation exposures. No personalized position weight is inferred from a valuation gap. SOURCES Evidence, dates and what remains unproven ↑ Actuals carry the issuer’s definitions and reporting dates. New forecasts and interpretation are TickerLantern judgments made 25 October 2026. Financial source confidence and readiness to own a security are separate: these articles provide watchlist valuation frameworks, not formally underwritten buy recommendations. Q3 weighted diluted shares are 701.7m. Reported TTM EPS is approximately C$12.27 versus adjusted C$14.38. A provider

documents.title: CIBC valuation & senior equity analysis
documents.description: Improved Canadian profitability and a steadier U.S. business strengthen the franchise. The valuation now requires those returns to persist after tax benefits, transaction charges and provision releases are normalized.
documents.body: Canadian banks / Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce CIBC: stronger returns, less room for an easy rerating Improved Canadian profitability and a steadier U.S. business strengthen the franchise. The valuation now requires those returns to persist after tax benefits, transaction charges and provision releases are normalized. TickerLantern Research 25 October 2026 Financials: quarter ended 31 July 2026 Watchlist · earnings durability versus price Can improved customer earnings and capital discipline outlast favourable markets and credit comparisons? Our FY2027 modeled EPS of C$11.56 and 13.5× exit P/E imply C$156.05 in October 2027 and a +0.5% cash-dividend-inclusive return. This is a conditional valuation case. The case at a glance CAD Reference close C$159.59 12-month model value C$156.05 FY2027 EPS · our model C$11.56 Base total return +0.5% Price: 23 October 2026 Financials: 31 July 2026 Analysis: 25 October 2026 Evidence confidence: high for cited actuals; forecasts are judgment. Underwriting: watchlist / scenario research. StockAnalysis TSX CM historical price · 23 October 2026 close Source posture Issuer reported and issuer-adjusted results stay distinct. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and review flags are TickerLantern assumptions. No licensed consensus feed or point-in-time valuation backtest is represented. VIEW Stronger profitability does not remove the entry-price test ↑ CIBC has earned a more serious profitability discussion. The research question is whether the improved return is sufficiently durable to justify a premium valuation after Canadian margin gains, strong market activity and easier U.S. credit comparisons. A favourable answer on the business still needs a separate answer on the price. At the C$159.59 TSX close on 23 October 2026, investors are paying for continued execution rather than merely the possibility of stabilization. Our central distinction is between recurring customer economics and the environment supporting them. Deeper commercial, wealth and household relationships can improve the quality of earnings. A favourable interest-rate mix, strong asset markets or provision reversals can also improve earnings quickly, but provide less evidence about performance through a full credit and market cycle. A reasonable multiple should reflect both kinds of contribution. The latest quarter produced 16.8% adjusted annualized ROE. Applying that return indefinitely would already be a meaningful assumption. The valuation diagnostic below asks what sustainable ROE would be required at the current common-book premium under an explicit cost of equity and growth rate. It prevents a high return quarter from becoming an unexamined justification for any share price. The upside case needs repeatable pre-provision earnings, disciplined losses and affordable capital distributions to reinforce one another. The downside can be less dramatic than a banking crisis: slower customer revenue, additional credit charges and a lower multiple can impair shareholder returns while CIBC remains profitable. Our stance is a valuation-sensitive watchlist, with the operating evidence determining whether a lower price or higher earnings would improve the case. StockAnalysis TSX CM historical price · 23 October 2026 close CIBC Q3 2026 earnings release · Highlights, segment commentary and non-GAAP reconciliations EARN Normalize the Caribbean charge and the tax benefit consistently ↑ Q3 reported EPS was C$2.47 compared with C$2.73 adjusted. The reconciliation removes C$232m after tax associated with the announced Caribbean sale and C$7m of acquisition-intangible amortization. Those exclusions help isolate the continuing operating result. They do not restore economic capital already spent or make the transaction irrelevant to shareholders. The year-to-date direction is different: reported EPS of C$8.22 exceeds adjusted C$8.03 because an earlier C$422m tax recovery is removed from adjusted earnings alongside the charges. Selecting the higher reported measure in one period and the higher adjusted measure in another would create an inconsistent and flattering earnings history. The trailing bridge uses the issuer-adjusted series throughout. Credit normalization is another part of quality, even though it does not appear in the issuer adjustment list. A release of expected-loss allowances is a legitimate accounting outcome. It also reduces the credit burden below a case that assumes no further release. Our operating forecast therefore makes the total annual PCL assumption visible, and the stress tool adds a separate credit charge rather than asserting that the latest credit outcome repeats indefinitely. Profitability must also be measured after claims on earnings senior to ordinary common shares. The model deducts preferred and other-equity distributions and non-controlling interests before dividing by weighted diluted shares. This avoids dividing total bank net income by the smaller spot common-share count. The rounding and denominator caveat is explicit because a sum of reported EPS periods is not an exact reconstruction with one common annual share weight. CIBC Q3 2026 earnings release · Highlights, segment commentary and non-GAAP reconciliations CIBC Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF pp.5,12,15–16,26,38; printed pp.2,9,12–13,23,35 OPS The domestic relationship bank carries the case; markets amplify it ↑ Canadian Personal and Business Banking generated C$948m reported Q3 income, Canadian Commercial Banking and Wealth C$619m, U.S. Commercial Banking and Wealth C$320m, and Capital Markets C$722m. These are segment net-income amounts before the common-share deductions in the group forecast. They identify the engines without implying that all segment returns have identical capital and ownership definitions. The domestic franchise needs to convert improved margins into durable customer value. Better deposit relationships can lower reliance on expensive marginal funding and create opportunities across borrowing, payments and advice. Loan growth alone is less persuasive if it requires concessions on pricing or weaker underwriting. The next results should show whether revenue expands alongside primary relationships and controlled acquisition and servicing costs. Commercial banking and wealth add a useful connection between operating businesses, owners and investable assets. That connection can support recurring fees, but market appreciation can enlarge the fee base without equivalent net customer flows. A slowdown in markets can affect wealth and capital markets together. Our model therefore does not treat each business as an independent source of diversification under every stress. The U.S. contribution requires special scrutiny because a reduction in commercial-real-estate risk and related allowances can support earnings while the underlying franchise is still rebuilding. A better test is pre-provision revenue after funding and compensation, the persistence of operating deposits, and the loss experience of the remaining loan book. Selling a troubled exposure can improve future risk without proving that the original lending decision created value. Technology investment should be judged through service, unit costs and loss control over time. Announced AI initiatives may improve productivity, but the forecast assigns no separate earnings premium to a technology label. A credible efficiency case needs expense discipline after implementation and maintenance costs, together with evidence that customer outcomes and controls remain sound. CIBC Q3 2026 earnings release · Highlights, segment commentary and non-GAAP reconciliations CREDIT A performing reserve release can mask a higher impaired charge ↑ The Q3 slide reconciliation separates C$612m of impaired provisions from a C$48m reversal on performing loans, leaving C$564m total PCL. The annualized impaired ratio was 40bp, while total PCL was 37bp. These are different measures: quoting the lower total as the impaired loss rate would understate the loss burden on borrowers already in difficulty. Impaired provisions increased from C$481m a year earlier. The stock of gross impaired loans reached C$4.024bn, or 0.65% of loans, compared with 0.56% a year earlier. This does not establish a broad credit breakdown, but it does require more caution than a simple story of falling quarterly total provisions. New formations, sales, write-offs, collateral and recoveries need to be read together. Capital provides capacity to execute the strategy, not permission to ignore the return on each use. CET1 was 13.4% at July, compared with 13.6% in April. Loan growth, risk migration, market movements and distributions can all affect the ratio. An earnings model cannot by itself determine how much surplus capital is truly distributable because it does not forecast each regulatory exposure or management buffer. The adverse path combines slower revenue with more credit costs and less flexibility to repurchase shares. Holding one variable constant can conceal that interaction. The sensitivity section therefore includes a combined downside, and the bear valuation allows the market multiple to fall as earnings weaken. A favourable path would show improving impaired formations without reliance on more generous reserve assumptions, alongside capital generation after funding the continuing business. CIBC Q3 2026 investor presentation · PDF pp.22–23,34; slides21–22,33 CIBC Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF pp.5,12,15–16,26,38; printed pp.2,9,12–13,23,35 CASH A measured dividend plus buybacks still needs an earnings foundation ↑ The declared C$1.07 quarterly dividend is payable 28 October 2026 to holders on the 28 September record date. Four equal future payments would total C$4.28 and yield about 2.68% at the reference close. That annualization is a modeling convention, not a board commitment to future payments. Waiting for a dividend does not create a free investment return because value leaves the company when it is distributed. The June NCIB permits up to 30m common shares from 8 June 2026 through no later than 7 June 2027, subject to its terms. The preceding 20m-share bid was completed and terminated. The current authorization is not proof that the new maximum has been executed. Each future reduction in shares must be funded from cash capital and evaluated against lending, investment and resilience needs. A repurchase above common book can improve EPS while reducing book per remaining share relative to retaining the cash. That arithmetic does not make it inherently poor allocation. The key question is whether the return offered by the repurchased earnings stream exceeds the return on alternative uses after allowing for risk. A high spot multiple makes that question more demanding. Our 12-month valuation uses a flat dividend assumption and the forecast share count already inside EPS. It adds no extra buyback yield to the return. The five-year tool is a separate illustration with editable dividend growth; it does not establish that the bank can maintain that payment path in every credit environment. Monitor common earnings, capital, share count and actual cash spent together. CIBC declares Q4 2026 dividends · PDF p.1 CIBC receives TSX approval for new NCIB · Opening paragraphs and bid terms StockAnalysis TSX CM historical price · 23 October 2026 close MODEL A linked operating forecast through FY2028 ↑ Forecasts begin with the issuer-adjusted nine months actually reported. We add an independently assumed Q4, then grow revenue and expenses separately, set credit provisions and tax, deduct non-common claims, and divide common earnings by diluted shares. Every FY2026 full-year column therefore contains an estimate. No forecast in this table is bank guidance or Street consensus. The assumptions that drive the result Q4 revenue of C$8.3bn is below Q3, with C$4.43bn adjusted expense and C$650m PCL. That deliberately avoids repeating the performing reserve reversal as a permanent credit subsidy. The forecast contains no repeated Q1 tax benefit or Caribbean disposal addback layered onto already adjusted earnings. FY2027 revenue grows 7% and expense 6%; FY2028 slows to 5.5% and 5%. The case requires positive operating leverage while keeping technology and control costs in expenses. It does not treat strong Capital Markets activity or AI-related productivity as an independently guaranteed growth stream. A 23% ordinary tax rate, explicit non-common claims and declining diluted shares are our assumptions. Annual PCL rises to C$2.7bn and C$2.85bn. documents.title: RBC Valuation & Senior Equity Analysis
documents.description: Royal Bank of Canada senior equity analysis: earnings forecasts through FY2028, credit, capital, dividends, valuation scenarios, ROE persistence, historical return research and interactive calculators.
documents.body: Canadian banks / Royal Bank of Canada RBC: strong franchise, limited valuation cushion Quality is priced in. Our issuer-adjusted FY2027 EPS forecast of C$18 and 15.5× exit multiple support C$279 in 12 months, a modeled 2.2% total return including dividends from the dated C$280.01 price. Independent senior equity analysis 18 October 2026 Original valuation 17 October · return study 18 October Methods and sources Neutral /watchlist · valuation-sensitive RBC’s scale,18.1% adjusted quarterly ROE and capital support a premium. The price already requires durable excess returns. Test the earnings mix, credit cycle and capital deployment before assuming that good business performance must produce a high stock return. Read the expanded investment case · Historical return study · Compare valuation assumptions Senior case at a glance CAD Reference close C$280.01 12-month model value C$279 FY2027 EPS · own estimate C$18.00 Base total return +2.2% Price:16 October 2026 Financials:quarter ended 31 July Forecast and exit multiple:our assumptions RBC Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF p. 14 StockAnalysis: TSX RY price and statistics Source posture Issuer actuals anchor our original operating forecast. Senior scenario weights and review bands are judgment; older provider-estimate cases and the historical return study remain separate. This is not a licensed consensus feed. VIEW The senior view: quality is priced in ↑ RBC is a high-return franchise with a strong Canadian banking anchor and significant wealth and capital-markets earnings. At the dated C$280.01 price, our base operating case supports only a modest prospective return. The question is how much persistence investors should pay for. Research stance Neutral / watchlist Valuation-sensitive; independent judgment 12-month model value C$279 October 2027 · FY2027 EPS 18 ×15.5 Base total return +2.2% Includes assumed C$7.04 cash dividends 10% modeled-return entry C$260 Unchanged base outcome; not a timing forecast Why the business deserves a premium Distribution scale, relationship deposits, Canadian banking efficiency and wealth referrals can sustain excess returns. Q3 adjusted ROE reached 18.1%, efficiency was 52.2%, and CET1 held at 13.5%. These are substantive advantages. Why the starting price matters Our FY2027 adjusted EPS forecast already grows 8.7%. Yet a still-premium 15.5× exit multiple gives C$279, close to today’s price. Strong operating results can coexist with an ordinary shareholder return when the starting valuation is demanding. What would change the stance? Durable EPS above C$19.5 with credit and capital intact would challenge our caution. Sustainable ROE below 16%, worsening client economics or rising capital intensity would weaken the franchise-premium thesis. A lower price improves value only if the earnings power survives. Analysis expanded 18 October 2026. Financials through 31 July; price 16 October. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and scenario weights below are TickerLantern assumptions. This is independent research, with no investment-bank affiliation or personalized suitability assessment. Positive and negative bars show magnitude; the signed value gives direction. RBC’s C$6.024bn reported Q3 income rose 11.3% year over year. Wealth Management and Capital Markets generated C$2.986bn,49.6% of group income. Both contain recurring businesses, but asset prices, activity and issuance can move together. Personal Banking income fell C$15m and Insurance C$50m, so growth was not uniform. Issuer-adjusted bridge: FY2025 EPS 14.43 − prior nine-month 10.58 + current nine-month 12.26 = TTM16.11. Q3 reported EPS 4.23 becomes 4.28 after excluding C$77m after-tax acquisition-intangible amortization; no HSBC integration-cost adjustment is present for this quarter. Why Morningstar revenue differs from the issuer The captured quarter shows revenue C$18.511bn versus issuer C$18.538bn. Its combined expense/other-income line is also C$27m lower. That C$27m equals joint-venture/associate income, leaving pretax income unchanged at C$7.749bn. Our operating model uses the issuer revenue/expense classification consistently. This is a presentation reconciliation, not evidence of an accounting error. Canadian NIM 2.96% and the group ratio excluding trading 2.07% help distinguish franchise economics from denominator changes. Commercial average deposits rose 9%; pricing and relationship quality remain essential. HSBC: the next increment is revenue execution Morningstar describes the C$740m cost-synergy target as achieved in FY2025, and a C$300m revenue-synergy objective by end-2027 with one-third realized in FY2025. These are provider-reported objectives. Existing savings are already in the earnings base; the forecast contains no separate acquisition premium or automatic addition of the full target. CNB can provide upside through better efficiency and deeper wealth/commercial relationships. We require recurring progress after necessary compliance and risk spending. A deposit increase bought through higher pricing would be less valuable than durable client relationships. Rising impaired loans alongside lower allowance/loan ratios deserve scrutiny, but do not alone establish inadequate reserves. Collateral, recovery assumptions and scenario weights are required. Housing averages are not the tail Residential secured lending totals C$479bn, with C$418bn uninsured. Calculated current LTV is 56% overall and 54% uninsured. Those averages provide context, not protection for every borrower. Personal Canada mortgage impaired PCL is 3bps; credit-card impaired PCL is 333bps on a much smaller C$27.3bn average balance. Loss severity and unsecured exposure matter alongside housing volumes. Greater Toronto 58% and Greater Vancouver 52% in the LTV table are LTVs, not geographic portfolio weights. How much capital is actually available? RBC’s 11.1% includes its countercyclical increment; OSFI’s generic large-bank expectation is 11.0%. Management’s operating range is 12.5–13.5%. Earnings added 80bps in Q3; dividends used 34bps, RWA growth 30bps and buybacks 21bps, leaving CET1 flat. Growth and distributions compete for capital generation. Liquidity adds resilience: LCR125%, NSFR112%, high-quality liquid assets about C$487bn against modeled 30-day outflows C$389bn. Leverage, resolution rules, stress buffers and approvals also constrain distributions. Capital strength does not prevent the equity multiple from falling. At 2.895× book, a buyback can raise EPS while reducing book per remaining share. Repurchasing 1% of starting shares at C$280.01 lifts EPS 1.01% with unchanged profit before lost interest, but reduces BVPS 1.91%. Accretion alone does not establish attractive capital deployment. FY2028 EPS 19.28 grows 7.1% despite credit costs reaching 6.0bn, about 48bps of our average loans. This is a late-cycle test, not an issuer loss forecast. Our 15.5× multiple retains a franchise premium while allowing some normalization from 17.38× issuer-adjusted TTM earnings. For a 10% total return, the same multiple needs EPS 19.42,7.9% above our base; or EPS 18 needs 16.72×. A C$260.04 entry would meet that hurdle to the unchanged base outcome. documents.body: Canadian banks / The Bank of Nova Scotia Scotiabank: a better bank still needs a sensible entry price The turnaround is producing stronger earnings, but a price near twice July common book already anticipates more. Canadian funding, international credit and capital discipline determine whether the recovery can persist. TickerLantern Research 25 October 2026 Financials: quarter ended 31 July 2026 Watchlist · turnaround versus valuation Can recurring returns rise enough to justify the premium after international reshaping and record market activity? Our FY2027 modeled EPS of C$9.56 and 13.0× exit P/E imply C$124.32 in October 2027 and a -0.9% cash-dividend-inclusive return. This is a conditional valuation case. The case at a glance CAD Reference close C$130.00 12-month model value C$124.32 FY2027 EPS · our model C$9.56 Base total return -0.9% Price: 23 October 2026 Financials: 31 July 2026 Analysis: 25 October 2026 Evidence confidence: high for cited actuals; forecasts are judgment. Underwriting: watchlist / scenario research. StockAnalysis TSX BNS price history · CAD130.00 closing price at 4:00pm EDT Source posture Issuer reported and issuer-adjusted results stay distinct. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and review flags are TickerLantern assumptions. No licensed consensus feed or point-in-time valuation backtest is represented. Investment case The turnaround is working; the valuation already expects more. ↑ Scotiabank’s investment debate has moved from whether earnings can recover to how much improvement shareholders already own. The TSX closing price was C$130.00 on October 23, 2026 . Against July book value of C$64.99, that represents approximately 2.00 times book. A successful operating recovery can coexist with modest prospective share returns when the starting valuation incorporates a much stronger franchise. The latest quarter provides evidence of execution: adjusted diluted EPS reached C$2.28 and adjusted annualized ROE reached 14.2%. Those results strengthen the case that the bank can earn an acceptable return on its capital. They also raise the burden of proof. Investors need to establish that the mix of margins, credit costs and capital-markets income can survive less favourable conditions before treating one quarter’s return as a durable earnings base. The historical bridge is useful because an annualized quarter and trailing earnings answer different questions. FY2025 adjusted EPS of C$7.09, less C$5.16 in the first nine months of FY2025, plus C$6.35 in the comparable FY2026 period gives approximately C$8.28 trailing EPS. The approximation combines different diluted share weights. At the price anchor, it implies about 15.7 times adjusted trailing earnings; multiplying Q3 by four instead would describe a run rate. Our central question is the sustainable return required to justify the price. A steady-state diagnostic using 10.5% cost of equity and 4% growth implies approximately 17% sustainable ROE at two times book. The diagnostic shows why the investment needs continued improvement beyond the latest 14.2% result. Clear evidence of stronger recurring returns would support the price; progress that plateaus near today’s profitability would leave limited room for disappointment. Scotiabank Q3 2026 results · HTML: Financial Highlights; Business Segment Review; reconciliation Scotiabank Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF pages 4, 6, 8, 40, 79; text tables; screenshots unavailable Scotiabank fourth quarter and FY2025 results · HTML fiscal highlights and medium-term objectives StockAnalysis TSX BNS price history · CAD130.00 closing price at 4:00pm EDT Earnings quality Separate recovery, accounting clean-up and a record revenue quarter. ↑ The first task is to retain both reported and adjusted earnings. Nine-month FY2026 reported diluted EPS was C$6.00, versus C$6.35 adjusted. The difference does not make the adjusted measure invalid; it identifies costs and accounting effects excluded from management’s presentation. Shareholders ultimately absorb losses recognised in equity or earnings even when the operating business is improving. The divestiture accounting requires particular care. The supplementary information attributes C$367 million of the nine-month common-income adjustment to divestitures after tax and non-controlling interests, alongside C$59 million of acquisition-related amortization. Mixing those numbers can produce an incorrect earnings bridge. The strategic question is whether the capital released and management attention recovered earn better returns than the businesses relinquished. Normalization also needs economic judgment beyond the issuer’s reconciliation. Record underwriting and advisory activity can be legitimate recurring business while still exceeding a reasonable through-cycle assumption. Wealth fees can benefit from market levels that subsequently reverse. A defensible model therefore retains the operating franchise, moderates unusually strong activity where appropriate, and recognises the costs required to maintain it. Mechanically adding back every inconvenient expense would overstate distributable earnings. The October update provides a practical test of consistent definitions. The expected C$55 million Chile deferred-tax-asset writedown reduces both reported and bank-adjusted fourth-quarter earnings. An analyst may separately examine earnings without that discrete item, but that would be an independently normalized measure requiring a visible reconciliation. The announced KeyCorp contribution also needs to enter the model once, with the associated funding cost already reflected, rather than being layered onto earnings that already contain it. Scotiabank Q3 2026 results · HTML: Financial Highlights; Business Segment Review; reconciliation Scotiabank Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF pages 4, 6, 8, 40, 79; text tables; screenshots unavailable Scotiabank Q3 2026 Supplementary Financial Information · PDF pages 4–7, 19, 35–39: adjustments, shares, average balance sheet Scotiabank fourth quarter and FY2025 results · HTML fiscal highlights and medium-term objectives Scotiabank KeyCorp contribution and Chile tax update · Opening three paragraphs Franchise and business mix Canada supplies the anchor; international execution decides the premium. ↑ Canadian Banking gives the investment a measurable operating anchor. Q3 revenue was C$3.646 billion, expenses C$1.674 billion and PCL C$498 million. Its net interest margin was 2.38% and ROE 19.4%. Those figures suggest that mix, funding and execution can create value without exceptional balance-sheet expansion. The next test is whether improvement comes with durable primary relationships and deposits, rather than a temporary gap between asset yields and funding costs. International Banking must be evaluated on consistent ownership and currency bases. Q3 income attributable to the bank’s equity holders was C$725 million, while the segment headline before non-controlling interests was C$766 million. Neither should be silently substituted for the other. The published comparison also shows the importance of foreign-exchange translation and divested operations. Investors need evidence of growth in continuing local businesses before capitalizing a favourable translation effect as operating momentum. The geography creates diversification and a more demanding underwriting problem. Mexico’s growth opportunity must compensate for trade sensitivity and credit risk; Chile’s inflation-linked mortgages require attention to borrower affordability; Peru’s improving portfolio still needs to demonstrate resilience across the cycle. Different country tax rates, funding structures and minority interests mean a dollar of segment profit can have a different value to common shareholders depending on its source. KeyCorp adds a different route to North American exposure. Scotiabank held a 14.9% interest at July 31 and accounts for it as an associate. This structure brings earnings participation without full ownership of the underlying franchise. It also introduces dependence on another bank’s underwriting, funding and capital decisions. The relevant question is whether the investment earns an adequate return after Scotiabank’s funding and capital costs, including under a more difficult US regional-bank environment. Wealth and capital markets can improve group returns, but their earnings mix should influence the multiple. Q3 attributable earnings were C$515 million in wealth and C$647 million in Global Banking and Markets. The premium deserves greater confidence when fee relationships persist through weaker activity. Scotiabank Q3 2026 results · HTML: Financial Highlights; Business Segment Review; reconciliation Scotiabank Q3 2026 Investor Presentation · Slides 4, 9, 10, 42, 47–49 Scotiabank Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders · PDF pages 4, 6, 8, 40, 79; text tables; screenshots unavailable Credit and capital Lower quarterly provisions do not mean the credit cycle is finished. ↑ Credit gives a mixed signal. The annualized Q3 PCL rate fell to 56 basis points from 66 in Q2, while the nine-month rate was 61 basis points. Yet gross impaired loans reached C$7.801 billion, or 1.00% of loans and acceptances. A lower provision flow can reflect better recent outcomes without establishing that the stock of problem exposures has peaked. The composition matters as much as the total. Canadian net impaired loans increased from C$1.860 billion to C$1.950 billion quarter over quarter; international net impaired loans edged from C$3.079 billion to C$3.093 billion. Investors should distinguish newly impaired borrowers, foreign-currency translation, write-offs and allowance changes. A stable aggregate ratio can conceal deterioration in a specific portfolio, especially where collateral values or refinancing capacity are weakening. Capital is adequate to support strategy only if deployment remains disciplined. CET1 was 13.1% at July 31, down 20 basis points sequentially. The presentation attributes the movement to retained earnings, RWA growth, a synthetic-risk-transfer recall, repurchases and currency effects. The lesson is that accounting earnings are not entirely available for distribution: business growth and risk migration can consume capital at the same time that shareholders receive cash. Credit sensitivity should be expressed through earnings and capital together. In an illustrative C$800 billion average-loan portfolio, 20 additional basis points of annual losses would cost C$1.6 billion before tax. The accompanying reduction in retained earnings would also narrow distribution flexibility. The thesis strengthens if impaired formations improve while capital remains resilient after growth and distributions. It weakens if provision relief precedes another rise in impaired assets or requires increasingly optimistic macroeconomic assumptions. Four times that amount gives a C$4.56 annualized run rate and approximately 3.5% yield at C$130. Neither is a promise of future dividends. The investment should be evaluated through earnings retained for growth and total distributions, because the headline yield alone does not establish an attractive prospective return. The October 2 NCIB amendment raised the authorization from 15 million to 40 million common shares, effective October 6. The bid continues no later than April 6, 2027, subject to its terms. This is capacity, not a completed repurchase. Repurchasing shares can raise EPS by reducing the denominator, but the cash committed has an opportunity cost. At a material premium to book, a repurchase generally reduces book value per remaining share compared with retaining the same cash. It can still create value if the stock trades below conservatively estimated intrinsic value. The argument therefore depends on purchase price, sustainable earnings and the alternatives available for that capital. The appropriate scorecard combines organic common-income growth, share count, book value per share and CET1. Management deserves credit when all four evolve consistently with better returns. A shrinking share count accompanied by weak underlying growth or pressure on capital would be less persuasive. Capital returned to shareholders is useful evidence of financial capacity; it should not substitute for evidence that the reshaped franchise can compound value. Catalysts and risks The next proof points are recurring returns and international credit. ↑ The next scheduled results release is December 2, 2026. The most useful evidence will be Canadian margin durability, customer funding, impaired-loan formations and the quality of capital-markets revenues. A headline EPS beat could be less informative than the components if it depends on unusually strong activity, currency translation or temporary credit relief. The October 21 announcement supplies two known fourth-quarter inputs: expected KeyCorp income of C$96 million reported or C$104 million adjusted, and the approximately C$55 million Chile tax-asset writedown. The associate income is reported with a one-month lag. The future benefit from lower Chilean tax rates should be assessed separately from the immediate accounting charge. International execution is the central operating catalyst. Evidence of improved continuing-business revenue, risk-adjusted margins and local-currency profitability would support confidence that the reshaping is producing more than an easier comparison. Mexico-related trade disruption, persistent Chilean mortgage stress or renewed corporate credit deterioration would challenge that conclusion. The buyback can amplify per-share progress, but international loan performance can overwhelm that benefit if underwriting deteriorates. The strongest falsifier of a cautious valuation view would be sustained returns materially above the latest quarter, supported by recurring fee relationships and book-value growth. The strongest falsifier of the turnaround thesis would be renewed credit deterioration alongside capital pressure and stagnant core income. At the current premium to book, investors should demand proof of the former while keeping explicit room for the latter in scenario valuation. documents.description: Capital return and a stronger earnings base support the franchise. A demanding starting valuation still requires durable U.S. execution, sound Canadian credit and lasting control improvements.
documents.body: Canadian banks / The Toronto-Dominion Bank TD: recovery has a price; controls still matter Capital return and a stronger earnings base support the franchise. A demanding starting valuation still requires durable U.S. execution, sound Canadian credit and lasting control improvements. TickerLantern Research 25 October 2026 Financials: quarter ended 31 July 2026 Watchlist · valuation and execution sensitive Can repeatable common earnings justify the recovery premium while U.S. constraints remain? Our FY2027 modeled EPS of C$11.19 and 14.0× exit P/E imply C$156.71 in October 2027 and a -7.6% cash-dividend-inclusive return. This is a conditional valuation case. The case at a glance CAD Reference close C$174.47 12-month model value C$156.71 FY2027 EPS · our model C$11.19 Base total return -7.6% Price: 23 October 2026 Financials: 31 July 2026 Analysis: 25 October 2026 Evidence confidence: high for cited actuals; forecasts are judgment. Underwriting: watchlist / scenario research. StockAnalysis — TD TSX historical prices · CAD174.47 delayed closing quote; observed October 25, 2026 Source posture Issuer reported and issuer-adjusted results stay distinct. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and review flags are TickerLantern assumptions. No licensed consensus feed or point-in-time valuation backtest is represented. The decision hinge The recovery is real; the easy valuation argument has gone ↑ Research judgment: TD is best framed as a capital-return and earnings-durability test. The investment case needs more than evidence that the franchise survived its U.S. compliance failure. At the October 23, 2026 TSX close of C$174.47, the shares trade at a calculated 17.86 times trailing adjusted EPS and 2.50 times July book value. That valuation already anticipates substantial recovery. It leaves less room for a thesis built only on improving sentiment. The central question is whether incremental earnings come from deeper relationships and a better operating model, or from favourable credit comparisons, buoyant markets and fewer shares. These sources can coexist, but they deserve different multiples. Customer relationships and repeatable service efficiency support a durable premium. Market activity and provision normalization can lift earnings quickly while offering less protection when conditions reverse. TD has an attractive route to value creation: retain the Canadian franchise, improve U.S. returns within existing constraints and distribute genuinely surplus capital. The combined route is more credible than assuming a rapid reopening of unrestricted U.S. expansion. The base underwriting should therefore allow operating improvement without assigning a removal date to the U.S. asset cap. A favourable business view does not automatically establish an attractive entry price. The valuation must still work after normalizing market-sensitive income, retaining a continuing control-cost burden and charging a sensible cost of equity. Upside requires earnings to outperform that disciplined baseline or a premium multiple to persist. Downside can arise from multiple compression even when absolute earnings continue to grow. StockAnalysis — TD TSX historical prices · CAD174.47 delayed closing quote; observed October 25, 2026 TD Q3 FY2026 earnings release · Financial highlights; Tables 1, 3, 5; segment discussions; AML update TD Q4 and FY2025 earnings release · Annual financial highlights and strategy targets TD global AML resolution — original SEC exhibit · Settlement terms and US$434 billion asset-cap scope Normalize the denominator Keep the recovery, remove the accounting shortcuts ↑ For the nine months ended July 31, 2026, adjusted EPS was C$7.59 versus C$6.19 a year earlier. The clean trailing calculation is C$8.37 for FY2025, less C$6.19 for its first nine months, plus C$7.59 for the latest nine months: C$9.77. This is a historical earnings measure. It is neither a forecast nor an assertion that the latest quarter can be repeated unchanged. The more revealing test is the bridge from revenue to common earnings. Subtract insurance service expenses from adjusted revenue, then deduct operating expenses and credit losses, apply tax, deduct preferred and other equity distributions, and divide by diluted shares. A gross insurance-revenue increase can overstate operating momentum if claims rise alongside it. Likewise, a lower share count can amplify EPS without producing equivalent growth in group profit. FY2025 reported earnings include the Schwab sale and should not anchor a recurring P/E argument. Equally, adjusted earnings should not become a licence to remove every inconvenient expense. AML remediation and related governance investments already burden the operating result. A model that adds them back again would create an earnings number that the published adjusted measure does not support. The forward model should preserve these distinctions. Allow a normal credit charge, avoid extrapolating a particularly strong capital-markets quarter indefinitely, and make tax and share assumptions visible. A conservative model can still recognize real productivity benefits. The falsifier is not simply a smaller adjusted-to-reported gap; it is a failure of common earnings to grow after the unusually helpful comparisons and repurchase effects fade. TD Q3 FY2026 earnings release · Financial highlights; Tables 1, 3, 5; segment discussions; AML update TD Q4 and FY2025 earnings release · Annual financial highlights and strategy targets Where returns are earned Canada funds the thesis; the U.S. has to earn its capital ↑ In Q3 FY2026, Canadian P&C earned C$2.095 billion, U.S. Banking C$1.074 billion, Wealth and Insurance C$841 million and Wholesale C$743 million. Those figures describe distinct engines. Treating TD as a single interest-rate exposure obscures the different operating risks, capital requirements and cyclicality underneath the consolidated result. The Canadian relationship bank is the anchor. The relevant question is whether deposit gathering, mortgage execution and business-client penetration expand together without sacrificing pricing or underwriting discipline. Volume growth purchased through aggressive rates would be less valuable than growth from customers using several products. Watch the relation between loan growth, deposit growth, margin and acquisition costs, rather than declaring victory from any one volume measure. The U.S. business requires a different lens. The asset restriction makes balance-sheet allocation and customer economics especially important. Shedding low-return assets can improve margins and capital efficiency even as total loans contract. But runoff is finite. Once that comparison is exhausted, the business must demonstrate healthier core relationships, better deposit mix and greater fee contribution. Faster reported growth against restructuring losses is a weaker signal than recurring operating improvement. Wealth, insurance and wholesale broaden the earnings base but bring their own sensitivities. Rising asset markets support fees; active financing and trading support wholesale; insurance claims can interrupt the apparent annuity. Diversification helps most when the engines respond differently to stress. The underwriting should not give every business its best environment simultaneously. Segment ROEs also use allocated capital, so their levels should not be read as directly interchangeable with consolidated shareholder returns. TD Q3 FY2026 earnings release · Financial highlights; Tables 1, 3, 5; segment discussions; AML update TD Q3 FY2026 Report to Shareholders — original SEC HTML · Report pp. 13, 25–30, 76 and 79; native HTML read TD global AML resolution — original SEC exhibit · Settlement terms and US$434 billion asset-cap scope Two distinct constraints Credit is improving; regulatory execution still governs the option value ↑ At July 31, 2026, CET1 was 14.3%. Q3 credit losses were C$917 million, with C$865 million impaired and C$52 million performing provisions; gross impaired loans were C$5.143 billion. These figures support a better aggregate credit picture. They do not establish that every portfolio has reached the same point in its loss cycle. The distinction matters because commercial resolutions can improve the group total while consumer migration worsens elsewhere. Provision releases and builds are forward-looking estimates, not cash receipts or losses already realized. The model should therefore distinguish the loss-rate assumption from loan growth and test both together. A weaker economy can raise provisions at the same time that slower lending restrains revenue, producing a disproportionate hit to common earnings. The separate regulatory issue is the U.S. bank subsidiaries’ US$434 billion asset cap established in the October 2024 resolution. It does not cover all TD businesses. Nevertheless, the constraint reduces management’s strategic freedom where controls failed. Capital strength can absorb costs and support distributions, but a high CET1 ratio cannot substitute for accepted remediation or authorize unrestricted U.S. growth. TD’s August 2026 update raised expected FY2026 remediation and related control spending to US$550 million and envisaged important work through 2027. Completion of management actions is only one stage; testing, sustainability and external review still matter. The base case should retain uncertainty after 2027. The downside mechanism is a longer period of elevated costs and constrained deployment, not merely another one-time fine. A fresh timetable or cost increase would warrant an immediate model review. Test whether core U.S. relationships improve as portfolio runoff matures, whether Canadian customer depth supports margin without undue pricing concessions, and whether fee businesses maintain acceptable returns when market activity is less generous. These are monitoring windows tied to subsequent results; no unverified regulatory milestone is treated as a scheduled catalyst here. Capital return is more measurable. Compare completed repurchases with the authorized program, average prices paid, diluted shares and the CET1 bridge. A reduction in surplus capital should be explained by distributions or productive deployment. Persistent excess capital with weak reinvestment returns would weaken the efficiency thesis; aggressive payouts accompanied by deteriorating credit or operating controls would weaken its resilience. The thesis would be materially impaired by another substantial remediation-cost increase, a longer validation timetable, persistent deterioration in core U.S. deposits, or consumer losses that outweigh commercial improvement. It would also weaken if market-fee softness exposed poor underlying cost control. None requires a solvency crisis to hurt shareholders: a premium valuation can fall as investors reassess the persistence of earnings. Conversely, the strongest upside proof would combine repeatable pre-provision growth, sound consumer credit, accepted control improvements and capital returned at sensible prices. That combination would support confidence in a durable return on equity. The research stance should change with that evidence and the entry valuation together. A higher EPS forecast alone is insufficient if the risk-adjusted multiple required to justify the share price has risen just as much.
